title: Balance Sheet Entries Can Count As Acknowledgment Of Debt Under S.18 Of Limitation Act: Supreme Court
case_name: Yusuf v. Vigyapan Loke Delhi Advertising CGHS Ltd
summary: The Supreme Court held that entries in a balance sheet could amount to an acknowledgment of liability under Section 18 of the Limitation Act, 1963, giving rise to a fresh period of limitation.

title: Being Natural Guardian Doesn't Entitle Father To Take Child's Custody By Force: Madras High Court
ratio: A father, though being a natural guardian of a minor child, cannot take the child's custody by force and should seek custody only in accordance…
summary: The bench of Justice AD Jagadish Chandira and Justice B Karthikeyan thus directed a father to hand over his 2.5-year-old minor child to the mother.

title: AI-Generated Books For Public Libraries? Madras High Court Directs DVAC To Register FIR, Directs Freezing Of Publishers' Bank Accounts
summary: The Madras High Court, on Tuesday (November 10), directed the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption to register an FIR in connection with the alleged scam in the procurement of books for public libraries. The court has also directed the authorities to take necessary steps to freeze the bank account of alleged fraudulent publishers.

title: Failure To Prove Penetrative Sexual Assault Warrants Modification Of Conviction: Tripura High Court Reduces POCSO Sentence
summary: The Tripura High Court has held that the prosecution's failure to establish penetrative sexual assault warrants modification of a conviction under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.

title: RTI | Information Sought To Examine Recruitment Fairness Can't Be Denied For Failure To First Establish Irregularities: P&H High Court
summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has set aside an order of the Haryana State Information Commission that refused to give an unsuccessful candidate the videography of the Band Skill Test in a Haryana Police recruitment.

title: Police Can't Restrict Licensed Bar Hotels' Operating Hours Merely Apprehending Drug Use: Kerala High Court
summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday (November 10) set aside the police notices issued to the manager of Kochi Radisson Blu hotel, an FL-3 licensed 5-star bar hotel, restricting its operation beyond 12:00 am and curtailing conduct of DJ parties after 11 pm.

title: J&K&L High Court Quashes FIR Over Railway Contract Dispute; Says Signing Agreement In Own Capacity Without Claiming Authority Is Not Forgery
court: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
summary: The Court held that an agreement executed by Mohd. Ashraf Beigh on October 16, 2021, could not be treated as a forged document merely because he allegedly lacked authority to execute it on behalf of a private construction company. The agreement itself disclosed that he was representing the company as the father of its Managing Director, and nowhere claimed that he held any independent authorisation to act on its behalf.

title: Calcutta High Court Dismisses Fresh Plea Against Demolition Of 'Illegal' Building, Says Pending Appeal Does Not Automatically Stay Court's Order
summary: The Calcutta High Court has dismissed a fresh writ petition filed by a man challenging an order directing him to demolish his allegedly illegal building, observing that the mere pendency of an appeal against the demolition direction does not operate as a stay of the order.

title: ITAT Kolkata allows depreciation on goodwill of ₹3,562.41 crore and other intangibles arising on demerger; Deletes ₹8.82 crore S. 14A disallowance

title: Onus on Uttar Pradesh to ensure undertrials allowed bail are released, says Supreme Court
summary: Of the 264 undertrial prisoners allowed bail, 106 had to continue behind bars for various reasons, including their inability to provide financial security or a guarantor to back them.
